sections.content: Nevada is a universal vote by mail state, which means all active registered voters will receive a ballot by mail and no request is necessary. Voted ballots must be postmarked by Election Day or received by 7pm if hand delivered.
Ballot curing is when a voter corrects an issue with their ballot, so it can be counted.

For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource. (http://nvsos.gov/sos/elections/candidate-information/campaign-finance-reporting-requirements)
Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here (https://www.vote411.org/ballot#.UFoDEFHh-Sp).

Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins on October 17th and ends on October 30th.

Early Voting Starts: 17 days before Election Day

Early Voting Ends: 4 days before Election Day

The next election dates can be found here www.VOTE411.org/nevada (https://www.VOTE411.org/nevada).

Contact your local Board of Elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.
Polling place hours of operation are from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm.

You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource (https://www.nvsos.gov/elections/election-information/2026-election-information/2026-polling-locations). If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your county clerk. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Nevada is a “closed primary” state. In order to vote in the primary election, voters must be registered with a political party. Unaffiliated or independent voters are not able to participate in the primary.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

To verify your registration status

  click here!  (https://nvsos.gov/votersearch/Index.aspx)

Nevada is now a vote by mail state, so all registered voters will receive a ballot by mail. You may opt-out from receiving a mail-in ballot if you wish to vote in person. Do not mail a ballot and vote in person. Voters who vote in person will have two options:

1. Early Voting - Early voting begins on 17 days before the election and ends 4 days before the election. Days and hours of operation vary by county. A list of early voting polling places by county can be found here (https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/elections/election-day-information). In order to avoid lines on Election Day, all voters who wish to vote in person are encouraged to vote early.
2. Election Day - Polling locations open at 7:00 am on Election Day and remain open until 7:00 pm. As long as you are in line by 7:00 pm, you will be allowed to vote. A list of Election Day polling places by county can be found here (https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/elections/election-day-information).
